cues.text: Let us now turn to section seven: risks and ethical limits.
Technology does not guarantee advantage.
Competitors can copy features, vendors can increase prices, and poorly designed systems can accumulate technical debt.
Technical debt is the future cost of shortcuts or neglected maintenance.
Think of it as a loan: a shortcut taken today saves time now, but you pay interest later in the form of harder changes, more defects and slower delivery.
Vendor lock-in is a related risk.
It makes switching expensive or difficult.
To mitigate it, use open standards, keep your data portable, include exit provisions in contracts, and design your architecture deliberately rather than by accident.
Next, consider algorithmic bias.
This occurs when data or decision rules systematically disadvantage groups.
For example, a lending model trained on historical approvals may reproduce historical exclusion, because the past decisions it learned from were themselves exclusionary.
To address this, test outcomes across relevant groups, review the quality of the data, provide human oversight, and allow appropriate appeals so that people can challenge decisions that affect them.
Cybersecurity failures can destroy trust and interrupt operations.
Beyond security, there are human and social concerns.
Workforce displacement and cultural resistance require training, communication and responsible transition plans.
Privacy, accessibility, affordability and digital exclusion matter particularly in emerging markets.
Consider a digital-only service that excludes customers without smartphones.
It may improve internal efficiency, yet it can undermine the business mission by leaving those customers behind.
Finally, how should an organisation balance innovation with reliability?
Pilot new services, measure the outcomes, limit rollout exposure, and maintain stable core systems.
And one important caution: do not confuse a successful pilot with evidence that a solution will scale.
A pilot shows that something can work under controlled conditions; it does not by itself show that it will work across the whole organisation or customer base.
